title: Transfer an uncaged HSR12X LM block onto a removing/mounting jig
objective: Bimanually butt a representative removing/mounting jig against an HSR12X rail, maintain parallel continuous support, and slide the uncaged recirculating-ball block fully onto the jig without losing a ball or contaminating or damaging the guide.
success_conditions: Full success requires physical end-face contact, parallel rail and jig axes, complete block transfer, all initially present balls still contained in four circulating rows, no impact, drop, contamination-zone contact, or unsafe inclination, and a stable one-second release. Safe jig mating and partial transfer may receive partial credit. Any lost ball, block jam, separated support interface, direct pose or velocity write, hidden weld, fixed ball, or collision suppression invalidates full success.
industrial_value: THK’s maintenance instructions prescribe a removing/mounting jig when block removal is unavoidable and require discontinuing use if a rolling element falls out. This makes preservation of the bearing elements an actual service outcome rather than an invented difficulty.
dexterity: One hand must keep a narrow jig physically butted and parallel to the rail while the other advances a small bearing block. The robot must regulate contact and regrasp without opening a gap that lets any freely simulated ball escape.

asset_plan: Author a representative full-scale HSR12XRM fixture using the visually verified A1-194/A1-195 drawings: 20 mm block height, 27 mm block width, 45 mm block length, 12 mm rail width, 11 mm rail height, and the documented four-row cross-section with end returns. Model every ball as an independent rigid PhysX body and preserve four physical circulation paths. Make the jig’s support cross-section continuous with the rail and clearly label its unpublished length, ball diameter/count, groove clearance, maximum transfer gap, and angular tolerance as prototype assumptions rather than THK specifications. Freeze those values before development and test ball circulation and loss, gap and inclination sensitivity, timestep stability, contact-force limits, reset freshness, and deliberate misalignment failures before YAM integration.
risk: The manufacturer drawings establish the selected model’s exterior, rail cross-section, four raceway rows, circulation through end plates, and lack of retention. Exact ball diameter/count, internal groove microprofile, jig length, and service tolerances are unpublished; these are bounded representative modeling assumptions requiring sensitivity tests and must not be presented as an exact THK replica.
